To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have defined a new fusion partner, the expressivity tag, that increases expression levels of heterologous genes in Escherichiae coli.
a 21 nt sequence of the translation initiation region of the InfB (infC) gene increases the expression level of heterologous proteins when fused to the C-terminus of the protein.
the expressivity tag is a novel tool for increasing protein expression in E. coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel tool for protein expression in Escheria coli, termed expressivity tag.
the expression of heterologous proteins in Escherichium coli.
the expression of heterologous genes in the model system Escherichia Coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
InfB(1) is an expressivity tag, which increases expression of a reporter gene and two proteins.
the InfB(21) tag improves expression levels in a manner that is not related to the function of solubilization or affinity tags, and that it is based on the translation initiation region.

the InfB(21) tag increases the expression of proteins by a mechanism that is not dependent on the codon adaptation index, codon usage or mRNA secondary structures in the 5'-end of the coding sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the InfB(21) tag increases protein expression levels by a factor of 5.
InfB(1)-based tags increase the expression level of the target protein by an increased rate of translation initiation.
InfB(1) is a fusion partner, that increases expression, but does not improve solubility or folding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 21 nt InfB sequence fused to a protein can increase expression levels.
InfB(1) is a novel tool for improving expression in E. coli.
the InfB(21) tag increases the expression levels of a number of proteins, and that this effect is independent of the fusion partner and is not related to codon usage or folding energy.
